title: Hamilton MicrolabAPI Alignment Primitive Schema
description: Shared alignment primitive for stating how one part mates with another, used across the Hamilton MicrolabAPI labware, site, and system schemas. An alignment is a named, located mating point; a feature (placeable side) and a receptacle (supporting side) that share a name are compatible, and the match positions the placed part by offset subtraction. Coordinate convention: left-front-bottom origin, X+ right, Y+ back, Z+ up. All dimensions in millimeters.
$comment: Shared sub-schema library, referenced by the labware, site, and system schemas through the major-versioned URN ('v1'); it has no documents of its own, so it declares its current version in the top-level 'schemaVersion' rather than per document. Additive minor increments keep the ':v1' URN so existing references stay valid; consumers validate against the current minor. Current target 1.0.0-alpha.1 (pre-release; structure may still shift). Consuming schemas place the same Alignment under two role-named lists — 'alignmentFeatures' (placeable) and 'alignmentReceptacles' (supporting) — so the role is given by the list, not by a field here. Match resolution (preference, then greatest resting Z, then declaration order) is a consumer algorithm, not a schema constraint.

Alignment.description: A named, located mating point relative to its object's origin. Carried as an alignmentFeature (how this part attaches to another) or an alignmentReceptacle (where another part attaches to this one). A feature and a receptacle that share a name are compatible.

name.description: Compatibility key — a feature and a receptacle with the same name mate (exact string). Bare snake_case is the shared cross-publisher vocabulary and the default (for example 'sbs_rim' or 'sbs_lid'). An optional 'publisher:' prefix marks a deliberately vendor-private mating (for example 'acme:cartridge_dock') that mates only the same publisher's parts; a shared mating must stay bare, since namespacing it would defeat the cross-vendor matching the vocabulary exists for.

rotationZ.description: Rotation about the vertical (Z) axis applied when this alignment is used, in degrees. The placed part's rotation is the receptacle's rotationZ minus the feature's; both default to 0, so the common case states nothing.

preference.description: Optional resolution override. When several alignments match, the match with the greatest summed preference (feature + receptacle) wins; equal preference falls through to the greatest resting Z, then declaration order. Default 0.

AlignmentOffset.description: Position of an alignment relative to its object's origin (mm). The coordinate frame remains the object's normal left-front-bottom origin; omitting X and Y means the consumer resolves them to the object's footprint center in that same frame, so the common case states only Z (the contact height).

x.description: X relative to the object's origin (mm). Omitted: the object's footprint center.

y.description: Y relative to the object's origin (mm). Omitted: the object's footprint center.

z.description: Z of the contact relative to the object's base (mm).
